names.official: Impuesto sobre la Renta de las Personas Físicas (tarifa estatal y participación local)

taxes.base: Employment, business, capital and capital-gains income of residents, after reductions and allowances.
taxes.payer: Individuals; employers and payers withhold it.

rate.headline: Combined State + regional scales about 19%–47%
details: The State scale for the general income runs from 9.5% to 24.5% and each community adds its own scale (the default scale is 9.5% to 20.5%), so combined rates are about 19% to 47%.
Savings income (interest, dividends and gains) is taxed on a separate scale from 19% to 30%.
The State tariff is half of the tax; a small municipal share (EUR 1.7 billion in 2025) is included here.

instruments.explanation: The largest Spanish tax. By law the income tax has two halves: the State tariff and an autonomic tariff that each community sets. AEAT figures show IRPF of EUR 142.5 billion in 2025: 66.4 billion State, 74.4 billion communities and 1.7 billion municipalities.
exceptions: The Basque Country and Navarre levy their own income tax under the Concierto and Convenio.

names.official: Impuesto sobre Sociedades

taxes.base: The profit of companies and other legal entities, after deductions and loss relief.

rate.headline: 25%; reduced rates for small companies
details: 25% general rate; 15% for newly incorporated companies in their first two profitable years; reduced rates for micro and small firms; a minimum effective tax of 15% for companies with turnover above EUR 20 million.

instruments.explanation: A State tax collected by the AEAT. Revenue grew 8.1% in 2025.

names.official: Impuesto sobre la Renta de No Residentes

taxes.base: Income earned in Spain by non-residents.

details: 24% for non-EU residents (19% for EU and EEA residents) on most income; 19% on dividends, interest and gains.

instruments.explanation: A separate tax on income that foreigners earn in Spain.

names.official: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido

taxes.base: Supplies of goods and services by businesses in Spain, and imports.
taxes.payer: Consumers; businesses charge it and deduct input VAT.

rate.headline: 21% general; 10% reduced; 4% super-reduced
details: The temporary reductions on energy and basic food ended during 2024–2025; the AEAT counts the return to normal rates among the measures that raised revenue in 2025.

instruments.explanation: The State collects all of it and passes about half to the communities and about 1% to municipalities as shares. The communities have no power over the rate.
exceptions: Health, education and financial services are exempt.

names.official: Impuesto sobre Hidrocarburos

taxes.base: Petrol, diesel, heating oil and other hydrocarbon fuels, per litre.
taxes.payer: Producers, importers and fuel distributors; passed on at the pump.

rate.headline: About EUR 0.47 per litre petrol, EUR 0.38 diesel
details: State rates of EUR 473 per 1,000 litres of unleaded petrol and EUR 379 per 1,000 litres of diesel; the communities may add a regional rate.

instruments.explanation: The largest excise duty; the State shares 58% of the excises with the communities as transfers.

names.official: Impuesto sobre las Labores del Tabaco

taxes.base: Cigarettes, cigars and other tobacco products.
taxes.payer: Manufacturers and importers; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: Percentage of retail price plus a specific amount
details: The rate rose in 2025, one of the measures that raised revenue.

instruments.explanation: The second-largest excise duty.

names.official: Impuesto Especial sobre la Electricidad

taxes.base: Electricity supplied to consumers.

rate.headline: 5.11% of the base
details: The rate returned to the normal 5.11% in 2025 after temporary reductions.

instruments.explanation: Revenue recovered strongly in 2025 as the temporary reduction ended.

names.official: Impuestos sobre el Alcohol y Bebidas Derivadas, la Cerveza y los Productos Intermedios

taxes.base: Spirits, beer and fortified wine by volume of alcohol.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: Per hectolitre of pure alcohol
details: Wine itself carries a zero rate.

instruments.explanation: Three of the excise duties on alcohol, reported together here.

names.official: Impuesto Especial sobre los Envases de Plástico No Reutilizables

taxes.base: The weight of non-recycled plastic in non-reusable packaging.

rate.headline: EUR 0.45 per kilogram of non-recycled plastic

instruments.explanation: A tax introduced in 2023 following the EU plastics levy.

names.official: Tráfico exterior (derechos de aduana)

taxes.base: Imports from outside the EU, by tariff heading.

rate.headline: EU Common Customs Tariff
details: Spain forwards most of the duties it collects to the EU budget.

instruments.explanation: Collected by customs; most goes to the EU.

names.official: Impuesto sobre las Primas de Seguros
names.native: Impuesto sobre las Primas de Seguros

taxes.base: Premiums of most insurance contracts.

instruments.explanation: A tax on insurance premiums that replaces VAT on insurance.
exceptions: Life and health insurance are exempt.

names.official: Impuesto sobre el Margen de Intereses y Comisiones de determinadas entidades financieras
names.native: Impuesto sobre intereses y comisiones de EE.FF.
names.common: Tax on banks’ interest and fee margin

taxes.base: The net interest and fee income of large banks and financial entities.

rate.headline: A percentage of the net margin
details: Introduced as a new tax in 2023–2024; the AEAT lists it among the measures that raised revenue in 2025.

instruments.explanation: One of the new taxes of recent years targeted at banks.

names.official: Impuestos medioambientales

taxes.base: Electricity generation, nuclear waste, hydroelectric use of water and other energy and environmental activities.

rate.headline: A different rate for each tax

instruments.explanation: The AEAT reports these taxes together as the environmental chapter.

names.official: Otros impuestos del Estado (transacciones financieras, servicios digitales, juego, gases fluorados y otros)

taxes.base: Financial transactions, digital services, State gambling, fluorinated gases, coal, e-cigarette liquids and other minor taxes.

rate.headline: A different rate for each tax
details: Financial transactions tax EUR 339 million, digital services tax EUR 410 million, gases EUR 104 million and smaller items.

instruments.explanation: The remaining State taxes, each below about 0.1% of national revenue.

names.official: Tasas y otros ingresos (capítulo III)

taxes.base: Public services and use of public assets: water canon, radio spectrum and others.

rate.headline: A different charge for each service

instruments.explanation: The AEAT counts fees in its total of tax revenue; here they are outside the national total because they are charges for a service, not taxes.

names.official: Cotizaciones a la Seguridad Social

taxes.base: Gross earnings of employees up to a maximum contribution base, and the declared earnings of the self-employed.
taxes.payer: Employers (about 30% of earnings) and employees (about 6.5%); the self-employed pay on their chosen base.

rate.headline: About 30% employer + 6.5% employee
details: Contingencias comunes 23.6% employer and 4.7% employee, plus unemployment, training and wage-guarantee contributions and the Intergenerational Equity Mechanism (MEI), which rises each year.

instruments.explanation: The second-largest source of revenue after the income and consumption taxes: EUR 176.9 billion in 2025, up 6.9%. The Intergenerational Equity Mechanism raised EUR 4.9 billion for the reserve fund.
exceptions: Civil servants have their own schemes (MUFACE, ISFAS, MUGEJU).

names.official: Impuesto sobre la Renta de las Personas Físicas (tarifa autonómica)

taxes.base: The same income as the State tariff, taxed again on the community’s own scale.

rate.headline: A scale set by each community
details: Each community of the common regime may set its own scale, personal and family allowances and deductions; the default scale runs from 9.5% to 20.5%.

instruments.explanation: The half of the income tax that belongs to the communities: EUR 74.4 billion in 2025. Several communities have cut their scale since 2022, which is a source of tax competition.

names.official: Impuesto sobre Transmisiones Patrimoniales y Actos Jurídicos Documentados
names.common: Property transfer tax and stamp duty

taxes.base: Transfers of second-hand property and other assets, and documented legal acts such as mortgage deeds.
taxes.payer: The buyer or the person who benefits from the deed.

rate.headline: Each community sets its own rate (about 6%–11% on property)
details: Property transfer rates differ by community (for example 6% in Madrid and 10% in Valencia); stamp duty (AJD) is about 0.5% to 2%.

instruments.explanation: The largest tax that the communities regulate themselves.
exceptions: New-build purchases pay VAT and stamp duty instead of the transfer tax.

names.official: Impuesto sobre Sucesiones y Donaciones

taxes.base: Inheritances and gifts.

rate.headline: 7.65% to 34% before regional rebates
details: The State scale runs from 7.65% to 34% and is multiplied by a coefficient for wealth and kinship; communities grant rebates of up to 99% or 100% for close relatives (Madrid, Andalusia and others).

instruments.explanation: A ceded tax whose burden varies hugely between communities.

names.official: Impuesto sobre el Patrimonio

taxes.base: The net assets of residents above an allowance.

rate.headline: 0.2% to 2.5% (State scale)
details: Communities set the allowance and scale; Madrid and some others rebate 100%. A separate State solidarity tax on large fortunes (ITSGF, 1.7% to 3.5%) applies on assets above EUR 3 million.

instruments.explanation: Ceded to the communities, which may remove it in practice with a full rebate.

names.official: Otros impuestos autonómicos (juego, medio ambiente, hidrocarburos tramo autonómico, matriculación y otros)

taxes.base: Gambling, environmental levies, the regional rate of the hydrocarbon tax, the vehicle registration tax and taxes that each community creates.

instruments.explanation: The rest of the communities’ taxes: OECD goods-and-services taxes EUR 8.6 billion and a few other items.

names.official: Impuesto sobre Bienes Inmuebles

taxes.base: The cadastral value of urban and rural property.

rate.headline: Each municipality sets 0.4%–1.1% (urban)
details: Legal range of 0.4% to 1.1% of cadastral value for urban property and 0.3% to 0.9% for rural property (TRLRHL art. 72).

instruments.explanation: The municipalities’ main own tax.
exceptions: Public property, churches and some others are exempt; municipalities may grant rebates.

names.official: Otros impuestos locales (IAE, IVTM, ICIO, plusvalía municipal y otros)

taxes.base: Business activities (IAE), vehicles (IVTM), construction (ICIO), increases in land value (plusvalía) and others.
taxes.payer: Businesses, vehicle owners, builders and sellers of land.

rate.headline: Set by each municipality within legal limits
details: The construction tax (ICIO) cannot exceed 4%; the vehicle tax has a legal scale by horsepower with municipal multipliers.

instruments.explanation: The remainder of local tax revenue by the OECD’s classification: income-type taxes EUR 8.9 billion, other property EUR 3.5 billion and goods and services EUR 16.5 billion.
